analysis: The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines ~621-625, base line 621). It describes an overlapped model-verification reader: a reader thread stays one 4 MiB chunk (WeightHasher.uncachedChunkBytes) ahead of SHA-256, using a second page-aligned buffer (OverlappedFileDigest). It states that verification still reads the same bytes and applies the same full SHA-256, and that existing fallbacks, page-cache dropping and the 'Any failed file prevents a successful aggregate' rule remain. No source code, config defaults, environment passthrough, authorization, attestation, key handling or cache policy is altered in the supplied evidence. Relevant threat areas are T-012/T-027 (weight substitution and weight-hash verification) and A-004. The doc claims no weakening: it only adds a performance and memory detail of two extra 4 MiB buffers per file hashed. I did not see the Swift implementation (WeightHasher.swift, OverlappedFileDigest), so I cannot confirm that the real code matches the doc. Specific points to check if that code is in another batch: that a short or failed read in the reader thread propagates as a hashing failure rather than a truncated digest; that the digest is still computed over the complete file in order; and that the two-buffer handoff has no race that could cause a skipped or duplicated chunk. Those are implementation questions outside this doc-only unit, not findings. Units 4 and 5 contain unchanged surrounding configuration text, and I identified no new regressions there. I did not re-verify historical entries.
